'''Igor Meglinski''' is a British, New Zealand and Finnish scientist serving as a principal investigator at the [https://www.aston.ac.uk/eps College of Engineering & Physical Sciences] at [[Aston University]], where he is a professor in [[Quantum]] [[Biophotonics]] and [[Biomedical Engineering]]. He is a [[Faculty member]] in the [https://www.aston.ac.uk/eps/engineering-and-technology School of Engineering and Technology] at the [https://www.aston.ac.uk/eps/engineering-and-technology/mechanical-biomedical-design Department of Mechanical, Biomedical & Design Engineering], and is also associated with [https://www.aston.ac.uk/research/eps/aipt the Aston Institute of Photonic Technologies (AIPT)] and [https://www.aston.ac.uk/research/hls/archa Aston Research Centre for Health in Ageing (ARCHA)].

== Background and Education ==
Meglinski obtained his BSc/MSc in Laser Physics from [[Saratov State University]]. In 1994, he became the first inaugural recipient of the 'Presidential Boris Yeltsin Award,' the most prestigious award for young scientists in the Russian Federation, supporting overseas study. This accolade facilitated his pursuit of a [[PhD]] degree in 1997, which he completed at the interface between [[Saratov State University]] and the [[University of Pennsylvania]] under the supervision of Professor [[Britton Chance]], Professor [[Arjun Yodh]], and Professor Valery V. Tuchin. His master's research involved the development of one of the earliest versions of the [[Monte Carlo method]] for simulating the propagation of laser radiation in tissue-like highly scattering environment, including the consideration of 3D macroinhomogeneities.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Meglinski|first1=Igor |editor-first1=Valery V. |editor-last1=Tuchin |title=Optical Methods of Biomedical Diagnostics and Therapy |chapter=Calculation of radiation intensity within biotissue with macroinhomogeneities |series=Proceedings of SPIE |volume=1981|pages=234–239 |year=1992|doi=10.1117/12.146473|chapter-url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377383865}}</ref> In the PhD studies he contributed to the invention and early development of [[Diffusing-wave spectroscopy]] (DWS) and its pioneering application for non-invasive monitoring of blood flow and superficial blood microcirculation ''in vivo''.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Meglinski|first1=Igor|last2=Boas|first2=David|last3=Yodh|first3=Arjun|last4=Chance|first4=Britton|title=''In vivo'' Measuring of Blood Flow Changes using Diffusing Wave Correlation Techniques|journal=OSA Trends in Optics and Photonics Series|volume=3|page=CM2|year=1996|doi=10.1364/BOSD.1996.CM2|isbn=1-55752-427-0|url=https://www.opg.optica.org/abstract.cfm?URI=BOSD-1996-CM2|url-access=subscription|archive-date=27 September 2022|access-date=28 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220927144003/https://www.opg.optica.org/abstract.cfm?URI=BOSD-1996-CM2}}</ref>

== Research ==
Professor Igor Meglinski is recognized for his pioneering studies on polarization optics in turbid scattering medium, which have fundamentally reshaped our understanding of light–tissue interaction. He played a key role in advancing biomedical applications of circular polarization,<ref>{{cite journal|last1= Kunnen|first1=Britt |last2=Macdonald|first2=Callum|last3=Doronin|first3=Alexander|last4=Jacques|first4=Steven|last5=Meglinski|first5=Igor|title=Application of circularly polarized light for non-invasive diagnosis of cancerous tissues and turbid tissue-like scattering media|journal=Journal of Biophotonics|volume=8|pages=317–323|year=2015|issue=4 |doi=10.1002/jbio.201400104 |pmid=25328034 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jbio.201400104|url-access=subscription}}</ref> polarization memory<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Macdonald|first1=Callum|last2=Jacques|first2=Steven|last3=Meglinski|first3=Igor|title=Circular polarization memory in polydisperse scattering media|journal=Physical Review E|volume=91|page=3033204|year=2015|issue=3 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.91.033204 |pmid=25871235 |arxiv=1502.07592 |bibcode=2015PhRvE..91c3204M |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevE.91.033204|url-access=subscription}}</ref> and Stokes vector depolarization composition.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Lopushenko|first1=Ivan|last2=Bykov|first2=Alexander|last3=Meglinski|first3=Igor|title=Depolarization composition of backscattered circularly polarized light|journal=Physical Review A|volume=108|article-number=L041502|year=2023|issue=4 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.108.L041502 |arxiv=2310.02632 |bibcode=2023PhRvA.108d1502L |url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevA.108.L041502 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> He  pioneered the use of orbital angular momentum (OAM) in complex tissue-like scattering media, demonstrating for the first time that twisted light can retain its topological phase structure after multiple scattering.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Meglinski|first1=Igor|last2=Lopushenko|first2=Ivan|last3=Sdobnov|first3=Anton|last4=Bykov|first4=Alexander|title=Phase preservation of orbital angular momentum of light in multiple scattering environment|journal= Light: Science & Applications|volume=13|article-number=214|year=2024|issue=1 |doi=10.1038/s41377-024-01562-7  |doi-access=free|pmid=39187516 |pmc=11347564 |arxiv=2312.08928 |bibcode=2024LSA....13..214M }}</ref> This work contributed to the emergence of a new research direction known as structured light diagnostics, which is based on the use of topological light modes. These studies were selected for publication in the [[Optics & Photonics News]] (OPN) 2024 Special Issue, which highlights the most exciting peer-reviewed optics research of the year, and were recognized for their potential to revolutionize non-invasive diagnostics using twisted light in clinical settings.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Meglinski|first1=Igor|last2=Lopushenko|first2=Ivan|last3=Sdobnov|first3=Anton|last4=Bykov|first4=Alexander|title=Orbital Angular Momentum of Light in Scattering Medium |journal=Optics and Photonics News |volume=35|page=43|year=2024|issue=12  |url=https://www.optica-opn.org/home/articles/volume_35/december_2024/extras/orbital_angular_momentum_of_light_in_scattering_medium/ |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In addition, continuing his research and development of [[Dynamic Light Scattering]] (DLS)-based imaging of blood flow,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Zherebtsov|first1=Evgeny|last2=Sdobnov|first2=Anton|last3=Sieryi|first3=Oleksii|last4=Kaakinen|first4=Mika|last5=Eklund|first5=Lauri|last6=Myllyla|first6=Teemu| last7=Bykov|first7=Alexander|last8=Meglinski|first8=Igor|title=Enhancing Transcranial Blood Flow Visualization with Dynamic Light Scattering Technologies: Advances in Quantitative Analysis|journal=Laser & Photonics Reviews|volume=19|year=2025|issue=2 |article-number=2401016 |doi=10.1002/lpor.202401016 |bibcode=2025LPRv...1901016Z |doi-access=free}}</ref> he is exploring hemodynamic patterns in postmortem mice brains.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Piavchenko|first1=Gennadii |last2=Kozlov|first2=Igor|last3=Dremin|first3=Victor|last4=Meglinski|first4=Igor|title=Impairments of cerebral blood flow microcirculation in rats brought on by cardiac cessation and respiratory arrest|journal=Journal of Biophotonics|volume=14|article-number=e202100216|year=2021|issue=12 |doi=10.1002/jbio.202100216 |pmid=34534405 |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jbio.202100216}}</ref> He discovered more accurate way of checking blood flow in the feet of type 2 [[diabetes]] patients,<ref>[https://www.photonics.com/Articles/Laser_Method_Boosts_Accuracy_of_Blood_Flow/a68797?refer=picks "Laser Method Boosts Accuracy of Blood Flow Measurements in Feet", PHOTONICS Spectra (February 2023)]</ref><ref>[https://www.aston.ac.uk/latest-news/aston-university-scientists-discover-more-accurate-way-checking-blood-flow-feet-type-2 Aston University scientists discover more accurate way of checking blood flow in the feet of type 2 diabetes patients]</ref><ref>[https://optics.org/news/14/2/18 Aston devises more accurate method to check blood flow in diabetes patients]</ref>
and pioneered using art to bridge the gap between complex scientific findings and the public.<ref>[https://www.aston.ac.uk/latest-news/aston-university-researcher-uses-art-help-demystify-complex-science Aston University researcher uses art to help demystify complex science]</ref><ref>[https://www.fenews.co.uk/student-view/aston-university-researcher-uses-art-to-help-demystify-complex-science/ Aston University researcher uses art to help demystify complex science]</ref>

Currently, he explores novel phenomena at the intersection of optical polarimetry,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Ushenko|first1=Alexander|last2=Sdobnov|first2=Anton|last3=Soltys|first3=Irina|last4=Ushenko|first4=Yuriy|last5=Dubolazov|first5=Alexander|last6=Sklyarchuk|first6=Valery|last7=Olar|first7=Alexander|last8=Trifonyuk|first8=Liliya|last9=Doronin|first9=Alexander|last10=Yan|first10=Wenjun|last11=Bykov|first11=Alexander|last12=Meglinski|first12=Igor|title=Insights into polycrystalline microstructure of blood films with 3D Mueller matrix imaging approach |journal=Scientific Reports |volume=14 |page=13679 |year=2024 |issue=1 |doi=10.1038/s41598-024-63816-z  |doi-access=free|pmid=38871757 |pmc=11176350 |bibcode=2024NatSR..1413679U }}</ref> actively contributes to the development of adaptive dynamic META-surfaces for 7D optical biopsy,<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Thrane|first1=Paul|last2=Meng|first2=Chao|last3=Bykov|first3=Alexander|last4=Sieryi|first4=Oleksii|last5=Ding|first5=Fei|last6=Meglinski|first6=Igor|last7=Diral|first7= Christopher|last8=Bozhevolnyi|first8=Sergey|title=Metasurface Polarimeter for Structural Imaging and Tissue Diagnostics |year=2025 |class=physics.optics |eprint=2501.05864 }}</ref> and advances quantum polarimetry for next-generation tissue diagnostics.<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Besaga|first1=Vira|last2=Lopushenko|first2=Ivan|last3=Bykov|first3=Alexander|last4=Setzpfandt|first4=Frank|last5=Meglinski|first5=Igor|title=Bridging Classical and Quantum Optics: Predicting Entangled Photon Behavior in Scattering Environments |date=2024 |class=physics.optics |eprint=2411.06134 }}</ref>

==Publications==
Professor Meglinski is author and co-author of over 450 scientific publications.<ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Igor-Meglinski-2/research Igor Meglinski Research Gate]</ref> His [[h-index]] is 56.<ref name="Google Scholar: Igor Meglinski">{{cite web|title=Google Scholar: Igor Meglinski|url=https://scholar.google.co.nz/citations?user=vQoHA10AAAAJ&hl=en}}</ref>

== Early Research ==
After a few years of postdoctoral research at the School of Physics at the [[University of Exeter]], Igor Meglinski joined [[Cranfield University]] in 2001 as a Lecturer and Director of the Biomedical Optical Diagnostics Laboratory within the School of Engineering. In 2007, he became the Head of Bio-Photonics & Bio-Medical Optical Diagnostics in the School of Health at Cranfield University. His research has primarily focused on a quantitative assessment of transdermal penetration of pharmaceutical and skin care product, and skin tissues chromophores and pigmentation by optical and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIR). He developed computational model of human skin for reflected spectra simulation.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Meglinski|first1=Igor|last2=Matcher|first2=Stephen|title=Quantitative assessment of skin layers absorption and skin reflectance spectra simulation in the visible and near-infrared spectral regions|journal=Physiological Measurement|volume=23|issue=4|pages=741–753|year=2002|doi=10.1088/0967-3334/23/4/312|pmid=12450273 |hdl=1826/885 |url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/0967-3334/23/4/312/meta}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Meglinski|first1=Igor|last2=Matcher|first2=Stephen|title=Computer simulation of the skin reflectance spectra|journal=Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine|volume=70|issue=2|pages=179–186|year=2003|doi=10.1016/S0169-2607(02)00099-8|pmid=12507793 |hdl=1826/884 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0169260702000998|url-access=subscription}}</ref> He also made significant contributions to the development of Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT), particularly in its application for skin and skin tissue diagnosis.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Proscurin|first1=Sergei|last2=Meglinski|first2=Igor|title=Optical coherence tomography imaging depth enhancement by superficial skin optical clearing|journal=Laser Physics Letters|volume=4|issue=11|pages=824–826|doi=10.1002/lapl.200710056|year=2007|bibcode=2007LaPhL...4..824P |s2cid=119375085 }}</ref> Additionally, he has conducted studies applying the Monte Carlo method for simulating coherent effects in multiple scattering.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Meglinski|first1=Igor|last2=Kuzmin|first2=Vladimir|last3=Churmakov|first3=Dmitry|last4=Greenhalgh|first4=Douglas|title=Monte Carlo simulation of coherent effects in multiple scattering|journal= Proceedings of the Royal Society A|volume=461|issue=2053|pages=43–53|doi=10.1098/rspa.2004.1369|year=2005|bibcode=2005RSPSA.461...43M |hdl=1826/896 |s2cid=53600398 |url=http://dspace.lib.cranfield.ac.uk/handle/1826/896 }}</ref> He was involved in the invention of an optical method designed for analysis and monitoring.<ref>[https://patents.justia.com/patent/20100304421 US 20100304421, S.A. Piletsky, I. Meglinski, E. Moczko, "OPTICAL MONITORING METHOD", published 2010-12-02, field 2008-11-06]</ref> This method can be applied to detect and monitor various changes in physico-chemical parameters, concentrations of analytes, and chemical and biological processes.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Moczko|first1=Ewa|last2=Meglinski|first2=Igor|last3=Bessant|first3=Conrad|last4=Piletsky|first4=Sergey|title=Dyes Assay for Measuring Physicochemical Parameters|journal= Analytical Chemistry|volume=81|issue=6|pages=2311–2316 |doi=10.1021/ac802482h|year=2009|pmid=19220044 |url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/ac802482h |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Since 2009, while at the [[University of Otago]] (New Zealand), Prof. Meglinski's research has expanded to include the development of a medical device combining multispectral optoacoustic tomography and ultrasound-modulated optical tomography.<ref>[https://www.otago.ac.nz/ctcr/news/new-light-on-cancer An excerpt from He Kitenga Horizons, a University of Otago publication (December 2013)]</ref> This innovative device is designed to provide clear, accurate images of tissue, with the ultimate goal of enabling cancer cell analysis at much earlier stages than currently possible with existing technology, and at a significantly reduced cost. As a Node leader in the World Consortium Biophotonics4Life (BP4L), representing New Zealand on the global stage of biophotonics-based research, Prof. Meglinski actively engages in the exploration of the fundamental properties of light and ultrasound in cancer diagnostics, collaborating with clinicians at the University of Otago Dunedin School of Medicine,<ref>[https://www.otago.ac.nz/ctcr/research/diagnostic-tools/igor-meglinski Centre for Translational Cancer Research]</ref><ref>[https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/grant-allows-cancer-research Grant allows cancer research]</ref> and with leading international scientists,<ref>[https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/laser-immunotherapy-treatment-hopes Dr Chen, of the University of Central Oklahoma, in the United States]</ref> while also being involved in the investigation of brain activity.<ref>[https://www.otago.ac.nz/__data/assets/pdf_file/0022/416038/download-issue-25-007177.pdf Biophotonics potential, University of Otago MAGAZINE, February 2010, page 31]</ref> He pioneered the application of circularly polarized light to distinguish between successive grades of cancer.<ref>{{cite book|last1=Meglinski|first1=Igor|last2=Macdonald|first2=Callum|last3=Doronin|first3=Alexander|last4=Eccles|first4=Michael |title=Optics in the Life Sciences |chapter=Screening Cancer Aggressiveness by Using Circularly Polarized Light |series=OSA Technical Digest (Online) |year=2013 |volume=2 |issue=9 |article-number=BM2A.4 |doi=10.1364/BODA.2013.BM2A.4|pmid=21991540 |pmc=3184856 |isbn=978-1-55752-966-4 |url=https://opg.optica.org/abstract.cfm?URI=BODA-2013-BM2A.4}}</ref> This work demonstrated that the phase shift of polarized light backscattered from biological tissue samples carries important information about the presence of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. In addition, in collaboration with his colleague, he developed a cloud-based online computational toolbox for the Biophotonics and Biomedical Optics scientific community,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Doronin|first1=Alexander|last2=Meglinski|first2=Igor|title=Online Monte Carlo for biomedical optics|journal=SPIE Newsroom|year=2011|doi=10.1117/2.1201110.003879|url=https://spie.org/news/3879-online-monte-carlo-for-biomedical-optics#_=_|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Doronin|first1=Alexander|last2=Meglinski|first2=Igor|title=Online object oriented Monte Carlo computational tool for the needs of biomedical optics|journal=Biomedical Optics Express|year=2011|volume=2|issue=9 |pages=2461–2469 |doi=10.1364/BOE.2.002461|pmid=21991540 |pmc=3184856 |url=https://opg.optica.org/boe/fulltext.cfm?uri=boe-2-9-2461&id=221167}}</ref> Nowadays, this toolbox is hosted at [https://www.biophotonics.fi www.biophotonics.fi] and is used extensively by a global audience of over 7500 users, including PhD students and young researchers.

In 2014, Meglinski returned to Europe, heading the Department of [https://www.oulu.fi/en/university/faculties-and-units/faculty-information-technology-and-electrical-engineering/optoelectronics-and-measurement-techniques#:~:text=Optoelectronics%20and%20Measurement%20Techniques%20(OPEM,as%20well%20as%20printed%20intelligence Opto-Electronic and Measurement Techniques] at the [https://www.oulu.fi/en/university/faculties-and-units/faculty-information-technology-and-electrical-engineering#:~:text=The%20Faculty%20of%20Information%20Technology,international%2C%20with%20over%2050%20nationalities Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering (ITEE)] at the [[University of Oulu]] in [[Finland]]. Utilizing advanced photonics-based technologies, emerging paradigms in machine learning, and new concepts in computational modeling of light-tissue interaction, Prof. Meglinski and his team at the University of Oulu developed 'Polarization Sensitive Optical Biopsy'.<ref>[https://site.fingenious.fi/en/articles/circular-polarization-in-cancer-tissue-diagnostics Finnish Biobanks and Biomedical Research News: Polarization Sensitive Optical Biopsy with Diffusely Reflected Light]</ref> This technique facilitates advanced diagnosis in cell cultures and screening of tissue samples, incorporating definitive pathology methods.Additionally, Prof. Meglinski and his team developed an [[Optical tweezers|Optical Tweezers]] (OT) based technology to investigate the impact of various nanoparticles on the mutual interaction of red blood cells.<ref>[https://phys.org/news/2019-09-tools-maneuver-medicine-carrying-red-blood.html Researchers experiment with tools to 'maneuver' medicine-carrying red blood cells, Science X, Phys.org]</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Avsievich|first1=Tatiana|last2=Popov|first2=Alexey|last3=Bykov|first3=Alexander|last4=Meglinski|first4=Igor|title=Mutual interaction of red blood cells influenced by nanoparticles|journal=Scientific Reports|year=2019|volume=9|issue=1 |page=5147 |doi=10.1038/s41598-019-41643-x |doi-access=free|pmid=30914741 |pmc=6435805|bibcode=2019NatSR...9.5147A }}</ref> This research demonstrates the potential of OT in studying targeted drug delivery systems, providing crucial insights into how nanoparticles can influence red blood cell behavior — a key factor in the development of effective and efficient drug delivery carriers.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Zhu|first1=Ruixue|last2=Avsievich|first2=Tatiana|last3=Popov|first3=Alexey|last4=Bykov|first4=Alexander|last5=Meglinski|first5=Igor|title=''In vivo'' nano-biosensing element of red blood cell-mediated delivery|journal=Biosensors & Bioelectronics|year=2021|volume=175|article-number=112845 |doi=10.1016/j.bios.2020.112845|pmid=33262059 |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0956566320308319}}</ref>

Since 2019 he is Professor in Quantum Biophotonics & Biomedical Engineering in [[Aston University]], working at the interface between [https://www.aston.ac.uk/research/eps College of Engineering & Physical Sciences] and [https://www.aston.ac.uk/hls College of Life & Health Sciences]. His research focuses on quantum biophotonics and biomedical engineering, where he has pioneered the application of [[Orbital angular momentum of light]] (OAM) for the quantification of exosomes and the exploration of intracellular communication.<ref>[https://royalsociety.org/news/2021/09/apex-2021-announced Orbital Angular Momentum of Light for Exosomes Quantification and Intracellular Communication, Interdisciplinary APEX Awards (2021)]</ref>
